rules.adoption: Adopted 14 Oct 2026 by the profile owner under Methodology v1.1. Drafted 2026-10-13 as a restatement of the mines profile for HouseBets' hilo2 from its published spec and the captured data.
rules.reproduction: Byte identity is required only for exact content. A pinned artifact's hash asserts the identity of the committed evidence — the dataset, the config, the seeds and the census (integer counts, round totals, integer-unit money) — and verify never rewrites it. A regeneration is written to outputs/run/ and compared with the committed artifact field by field: integers and strings exact; non-integer numbers within |Δ| ≤ 1e-14 + 1e-12·max(|a|,|b|), or the per-field tolerance a step declares; the diff records the runtime version and must be empty beyond tolerance. Run metadata is absent, not excluded. No verdict-bearing comparison turns on a difference below its declared tolerance. Shared with the Plinko profile (rules.reproduction).
rules.applicability: A check applies unless its `applies` predicate over the declaration is false. The engine evaluates the predicate; a false result prints the step as n/a with the derived reason (path, declared value) and the declared value is verified against the dataset or pinned config by the rule in `declarationTruth` (conformance C-13). A declaration never asserts n/a directly; `notApplicable` lists are ignored from 1.0.2.

numbering: Shared with the Mines profile: HILO-nn is the same property as MINES-nn for the core checks (01-05, 09, 11, 16, 23, 26-30, copied verbatim); slots 06-08, 10, 12-15, 17-22, 24-25 are restated for hilo; HILO-31, HILO-32 are game-specific additions. Template-only extras not carried: none.

policies.HARD_FAIL: any violation → NOT PROVABLY FAIR; verify exits 1
policies.FLAG: violation is disclosed with a limitation row; verify exits 2. A FLAG carries an origin: operator (Conditional Pass) or capture (limitation row, verdict class unchanged). Decided 2026-09-17.
policies.INFORMATIONAL: reported with its statistic and its reading, never affects the verdict and is never counted as a flag, whatever the statistic says; verify's exit code does not depend on it. The live-sample fit (check 22) is informational everywhere.
policies.RELEASE_GATE: package check that blocks publication when it fails; it never changes the verdict
policies.GRADED: not verdict-bearing; scored 1–5 in the QA scorecard and gated at release by the conformance floor

statusLegend.implemented: the check exists as specified and uses the declared parameters
statusLegend.partial: the check exists but is weaker than the profile (what is missing is stated)
statusLegend.missing: no step or package item covers it
statusLegend.n/a-declared: the casino's design makes it inapplicable; the declaration says why and the step prints it

checks.name: Seed hash integrity
checks.asserts: Every revealed server seed hashes to its published commitment under the declared encoding; the number of seeds checked equals the code constant for the audited population, not a count read from the dataset.

checks.name: Forward commitment chain
checks.asserts: For every rotation, the next-seed hash published before the rotation equals the active hash after it, and a pre-capture link anchors the chain before epoch 0. Recomputed from raw fields, never from a capture-script boolean.
checks.floor: All rotation events — zero unverified transitions
checks.declarationTruth: no key matching /next.*hash/i on any epoch record when declared null

checks.name: Hash consistency within epoch
checks.asserts: All bets sharing an epoch carry the same server-seed hash and the same client seed.

checks.name: Nonce continuity
checks.asserts: Within every epoch the nonces are exactly base … base+epochSize−1 with no gap, repeat or reorder; the base is a declared constant, not the minimum observed. An operator-side gap or repeat is a HARD FAIL; an auditor-side capture retry is a FLAG with origin = capture (limitation row, verdict class unchanged — decided 2026-09-17).
checks.floor: Nonce gap or repeat within an epoch → hard fail (methodology S1)

checks.name: Population & epoch size (G-BIND)
checks.asserts: Bets, seeds, epochs and per-phase counts equal constants in src/, every epoch has exactly epochSize bets, and the dataset's own totals are not the denominator; a secondary dataset file (e.g. a Phase E file) is pinned and counted the same way.

checks.name: Client-seed influence & Phase D recomputation
checks.asserts: A wrong client seed changes the turned cards at the rate the model predicts (0 % change → hard fail), an empty-seed control is run and its server answer recorded, every Phase D round with a player-set seed recomputes, predictable Phase D seeds are disclosed with the exposed epochs enumerated, and the A–C generator is disclosed and is a CSPRNG.
checks.floor: Client seed not used in computation → hard fail (methodology S2); Phase D ≥ 2 distinct client seeds
checks.declarationTruth: no record labelled phase D when declared 0

checks.name: Card-stream recomputation
checks.asserts: Every round with a revealed seed recomputes its turned cards: the k-th card turned after the start card (by a guess or a skip) is stream card k − 1, the stream being HMAC-SHA256(serverSeed, clientSeed:nonce:i) read as big-endian u32s with every u32 ≥ 4294967248 skipped and card = u32 mod 52; the start card is not from the stream and equals the bet's start card; coverage equals expectedBets; a skipped round is a FAIL. Spec: the operator's published fairness endpoint (/hilo2/fairness, 12 Oct).
checks.floor: Every bet individually recomputed; a single mismatch is a hard fail

checks.name: Draw bias bound
checks.asserts: Rejection at 2^32 − (2^32 mod 52) = 4294967248 makes every card exactly uniform on 0 … 51; the step prints the threshold derivation and the rejection census of the run.
checks.floor: Modulo bias exceeding 1/2^32 without rejection sampling → hard fail (methodology S2)

checks.name: RNG reference vectors
checks.asserts: Unit tests reproduce captured bets from their revealed seeds and fixed vectors against the operator's published algorithm or source; the adapter cites the operator source line it ports.

checks.name: Guess resolution & round sequence
checks.asserts: For every step: the guess resolves by the published button table for the rank shown (2 … Q: higher-or-same wins on 13 − r ranks, lower-or-same on r + 1; A: higher (12) | same (1); K: same (1) | lower (12)), a tie wins an "or same" guess, a wrong guess ends the round paying nothing, a skip turns the next card and never changes the multiplier, and a round shows at most 52 cards; asserted from the recomputed cards, never from the operator's outcome label. Spec: the operator's published fairness endpoint (/hilo2/fairness, 12 Oct).

checks.name: Payout arithmetic
checks.asserts: payout = amount × multiplier for every win and 0 for every loss, compared exactly on the declared money grid or settlement rule when one exists, otherwise within an absolute tolerance no looser than 1e-8; when the capture carries no payout field, the wallet delta is the payout and its resolution is declared.
checks.floor: Payout arithmetic error exceeding 1e-8 → hard fail (methodology S3)

checks.name: Bet-size invariance (Phase C)
checks.asserts: Every elevated-stake round recomputes identically and pays by the same formula as its base-stake round; Phase C guesses once on the likelier side so ≥ 100 elevated-stake wins exercise the payout path. HouseBets plan: ~200 rounds at 100 × the base stake (2.00) and 200 at $10.
checks.floor: Phase C ≥ 100 bets at elevated stake
checks.declarationTruth: no record labelled phase C when declared 0

checks.name: Multiplier formula & provenance
checks.asserts: After right guesses on cards where n_1 … n_k of the 13 ranks win, the served multiplier equals 99/100 × Π 13/n_i cut to 8 decimals and the payout is floor(stake × multiplier) on the 1e-8 grid, rounded down once; the published first-guess values (hiFirst / loFirst per rank) equal the formula; the formula's origin is the operator's fairness endpoint; no operator-supplied odds field is read by the derivation. Spec: the operator's published fairness endpoint (/hilo2/fairness, 12 Oct).

checks.name: Multiplier monotonicity & bounds
checks.asserts: The multiplier rises with every right guess and a skip leaves it unchanged; the published caps hold — a right guess that reaches the max win cashes the round out at that amount, and so does a right guess on the 52nd card; a cap branch not witnessed in data is declared unwitnessed; a violation is disclosed, not failed.

checks.name: Start-card, side & depth coverage
checks.asserts: Phase A covers every start rank and both sides with at least the floor; the multi-guess phase covers several depths, skips and cash-out points; coverage is asserted against the plan in code.
checks.floor: All published configurations; Phase A ≥ 50 rounds per start rank

checks.name: Wallet / balance reconciliation
checks.asserts: When the capture carries a balance field, every consecutive-bet delta equals payout − amount exactly (or within the declared truncation resolution) or belongs to a structurally recognised deferred-credit pair; otherwise the step prints n/a — declared.
checks.declarationTruth: no key matching /balance|wallet/i on any bet record when declared null

checks.name: Multi-guess parity
checks.asserts: Multi-guess rounds are captured with the value after each step; every intermediate value and the cash-out equal the formula at that depth; the card sequence is fixed before the first guess — every step's cards are a prefix of the settled cards; a skip never changes the multiplier.
checks.declarationTruth: no round with more than one guess request in the dataset when declared false

checks.name: Anti-circularity (win probability)
checks.asserts: The chance a guess on n winning ranks is right is n/13 from the infinite-deck model (every card drawn independently, 1 in 13 per rank), checked by enumeration over the 13 ranks for every button; no operator-supplied win-chance field is read; a negative control shows a corrupted card is rejected.
checks.floor: Config probabilities diverge from independent computation → hard fail (methodology S4)

checks.name: Effective RTP vs claim
checks.asserts: RTP is derived in exact arithmetic per (start rank, side, depth) from n/13 and the cut-to-8-decimals multiplier and compared with the published claim ("99% at any cash-out depth, from any start card, on either side"); a cell whose derived RTP differs from the claim — including the effect of the 8-decimal cut — is a FLAG with the magnitude; the per-cell table is published.

rtpClaimRule.enforcedBy: RTP_CLAIM_RULE_ENFORCED in each package's own src/rtp-claim-switch.ts, true since rule 1.2.0. The rule itself is core/rtp-claim.ts, which every package carries as a byte-identical copy (src/rtp-claim.ts); conformance C-13 compares SHA-256s and reports the package's switch value; bin/sync-rtp-claim.mjs re-vendors the rule and creates a missing switch file with false, never overwriting one.
rtpClaimRule.whileNotEnforced: the package computes the full per-setting exact RTP table, commits it (outputs/rtp-claim-table.json, SHA-256 pinned in src/rtp-settings.ts) and prints the rule's outcome as INFO; this check's own policy and every verdict are unchanged. A committed table that no longer equals the run or its pin exits 1 either way (it is evidence, not the claim).
rtpClaimRule.whenEnforced: 1.2.0: an outcome of FAIL (a setting more than the band below the stated figure, house side) is the package verdict RTP FIGURE OVERSTATED, exit 5: a fail until the casino fixes the figure or the paytable, never printed as NOT PROVABLY FAIR and never a Pass, because the draws themselves pass. Verdict and exit come from rtpClaimVerdict (draw fail 1 > INCOMPLETE 3 > RTP FIGURE OVERSTATED 5 > Conditional 2 > Full 0). NO_CLAIM, NOTED and PUBLISHED are never a miss. A committed table that no longer equals the run or its pin is a reproduction failure, exit 1.
rtpClaimRule.text: The casino can publish either (1) a single number ("99% rtp") — every setting has to be within the band of it; or (2) a range ("rtp 98.65–99.07% depending on settings"), anywhere findable, fairness page or rules is fine — every setting has to sit inside it, and the range has to be the real one: bottom = their actual worst setting, top = their actual best (within the band); no "up to 99%", no range wider than reality. Our audit publishes the full per-setting table. 1.1.0: the claim is the figure shown to players, on the game page, fairness page or help page; a game with no shown figure is marked no claim (kind "none", its source naming the game page, the fairness page and the help page and saying "no RTP figure") and still gets its full per-setting table: outcome NO_CLAIM, never a FAIL, no house-side failures. 1.2.0: six places count (game page, fairness page, help page, bet panel, rules, game settings); an edge stated in the game settings counts as stated, no screenshot needed; claims may be per-setting or tiered (each stake tier held to the edge the casino states for it); a zero-edge or promotional line is noted, not tested; a casino that publishes the real per-setting figures is PUBLISHED, but a bare paytable is not.
rtpClaimRule.band: 0.1 pp (RTP_CLAIM_BAND = 0.001 as a fraction of 1). A setting within 0.1 pp of what the casino states passes; past that on the house side is a FAIL; player-favourable never fails. For a range claim the published bottom may not sit more than 0.1 pp below the true worst setting, nor the published top more than 0.1 pp above the true best.
rtpClaimRule.arithmetic: exact rationals (bigint) for every setting, the claim and the band; an RTP a package can only derive numerically (a recursive EV engine, a double convolution) enters as the exact binary value of that double, and the package states the figure's precision.
rtpClaimRule.industryContext: GLI-11 v2.0 §4.4.1(b) requires the minimum RTP to be met "at all times … at the lowest end of a non-linear paytable", naming keno spot combinations; the lab reports the minimum and maximum theoretical payout.

checks.name: Simulation Pass 1 (fresh seeds)
checks.asserts: ≥ 2,000,000 card draws on pinned fresh seeds for card-id uniformity over 52 and serial independence, plus ≥ 1,000,000 rounds per first-guess class (start rank × side) for RTP convergence; statistics re-derived in verify from the artifact's rows; the committed experiment is pinned and replayable — census byte-for-byte, derived statistics within the reproduction tolerance (rules.reproduction).
checks.floor: Hilo reading of the 1,000,000-rounds-per-config floor (PROPOSED, for the profile owner): ≥ 2M cards + ≥ 1M rounds per start rank × side

checks.name: Simulation Pass 2 (cherry-pick)
checks.asserts: Every revealed seed × 10,000 nonces; early window = the captured nonce range; the statistic is the return of the guesses the casino actually served in that epoch against their exact mean and variance, with an exact or bootstrap null; every window re-derived in verify; pre-registered rule; detection power printed.

checks.name: Live-sample fit
checks.asserts: Captured turned cards fit the uniform 52-card law (1 in 13 per rank); informational.

checks.name: S5 fairness-integrity matrix
checks.asserts: exploit-testing.md carries the standardized matrix with framework IDs S5-1 … S5-8, each row Pass / Flag / Hard Fail / Not tested — disclosed, tied to a step or a capture.
checks.floor: All tests in the standardized matrix

checks.name: Player-verifier parity
checks.asserts: The site verifier's derive.js for this casino is generated from (or hash-matched to) the adapter's computeCards; the package records that hash.
checks.declarationTruth: cite resolves; when published is false the step prints n/a and the limitations register (HILO-30) carries the row

checks.name: Player check path documented
checks.asserts: README states, in order, how a player verifies one of their own rounds: where the seed is revealed, which fields to paste, the commitment encoding, the card stream (skip threshold, card = u32 mod 52, suit and rank), that the start card is not from the stream, the button table and the multiplier — using the declaration's field names.

checks.name: Dataset & config pins
checks.asserts: The live SHA-256 of every dataset file (master and secondary) equals the constant pinned in src/; the verifier aborts on mismatch before any step runs.

checks.name: Artifacts of record
checks.asserts: Every artifact the report quotes is pinned in src/, un-ignored by name, carries no run metadata, is never rewritten by verify (verify writes only to outputs/run/), and every numeric leaf has a declared value domain; the pin asserts the identity of the committed evidence, and byte identity across machines is required only for exact content — dataset, config, seeds, census — while derived statistics are compared at the reproduction tolerance, never by bytes (rules.reproduction).

checks.name: Fresh-clone reproduction
checks.asserts: On a fresh clone, npm ci && npm test prints N/N with the Full Pass verdict and exit 0 within the budget, without modifying any pinned artifact; a regeneration (test:full) is written to outputs/run/ and compared with the committed artifacts field by field — integers and strings exact, non-integer numbers within |Δ| ≤ 1e-14 + 1e-12·max(|a|,|b|) or the per-field tolerance a step declares — with the diff and the runtime version recorded in outputs/run/diff.json and nothing beyond tolerance; step counts in README/MANIFEST equal the suite; the audit ID is assigned; the runtime is pinned.

checks.name: Mutation battery
checks.asserts: A step-named mutation registry runs in a disposable copy; every scored step has at least one mutation that kills it; declared survivors are tied to limitation IDs; forged-evidence batteries are included.

checks.name: Disclosure register & evidence appendix
checks.asserts: MANIFEST carries the declared-limitations register with closure evidence, the load-bearing premises marked ASSUMED where unwitnessed, and evidence.md numbers every exhibit from E01 with its evidential role; no internal QA material ships in the package.

checks.name: Start-card carry-over
checks.asserts: The start card is not drawn from the round's stream: it carries over from the player's last round or from a free skip before the bet. The package checks that each round's start card equals the card the player was shown (the previous round's last card, or the free skip's card), and that the published claim "any start card is worth the same" holds by the RTP-per-start-rank table (HILO-19). A carry-over not witnessed in data is declared.

checks.name: Abandoned-round rule (24 h)
checks.asserts: The published rule "a round left without a decision for 24 hours is finished by the server: a round that can cash out is cashed out at its value; otherwise the card showing is guessed on its likelier side (hi on a tie of chances) and, if the guess is right, the round is cashed out" is tested on a deliberately abandoned round: the server-finished round is revealed and recomputed, its settlement equals the published branch, and the time from leaving it to the server's settlement is printed. A branch not exercised is declared unwitnessed.
checks.declarationTruth: no 24-hour / abandoned-round rule on the operator's fairness page when declared false
